title: Compressed OSCORE round-trip
notes: BLOCKED 2026-08-26 Phase-2 audit (no claim, no source edits): prerequisite project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.12.3.1 (Rule 5 compression) remains open. More importantly, project-LICHEN-worker6-jftb is still in_progress for a correctness defect in the Rust Rule 5 matcher: it accepts fe80::/10 while decompression reconstructs fe80::/64, so valid non-/64 link-local packets can be silently changed and an end-to-end compressed OSCORE round-trip cannot yet be certified. Canonical Rules 5/6 packet-level vectors are independently verified by closed sibling 12.3.3, but repository search found only separate OSCORE protect/unprotect tests and separate SCHC compress/decompress tests—not a production OSCORE -> IPv6/UDP/CoAP -> Rule 5 -> restore -> OSCORE integration consumer. Exact integration targets are also shared dirty (python/src/lichen/crypto/oscore.py, python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py, rust/lichen-oscore/**, rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs, OSCORE/SCHC tests/vectors). Current sibling agents reported no active edits, but the unresolved claimed jftb lane owns the necessary Rule 5 correction. Closed vector sibling also records an excluded Zephyr/C Rule 6 mismatch (C test uses fd00:: instead of the specified 0200::/8). Leave this bead open/unassigned until Rule 5 correctness lands, then add an independent Python/Rust cross-layer integration test using production consumers.
